status_summary: On 2025-01-20 Executive Order 14165 directed DHS to end the categorical parole processes for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans and Venezuelans, and Executive Order 14159 limited parole to case-by-case use. DHS terminated the CHNV parole processes by notice published 2025-03-25 and terminated the Family Reunification Parole processes for Colombians, Cubans, Ecuadorians, Guatemalans, Haitians, Hondurans and Salvadorans by notice published 2025-12-15. DHS terminated the 2023 Venezuela TPS designation by notice of 2025-02-05 (about 348,202 registrants), and on 2026-06-25 the Supreme Court ruled 6 to 3 in Mullin v. Doe that courts cannot review non-constitutional challenges to TPS decisions, allowing the Haiti and Syria terminations to proceed. A law-firm summary dated 2026-06-30 lists terminations for 14 designations; it reports that the Burma, Ethiopia, Somalia, South Sudan and Yemen terminations were under district-court stays that the ruling puts at risk, that the Ninth Circuit on 2026-02-09 stayed an order that had vacated the Honduras, Nicaragua and Nepal terminations, and that a court order preserved work authorization for a defined group of Venezuela (2023 designation) holders through 2026-10-02. A news report of 2026-09-10 (UnoTV, citing CNN) says DHS published no extension or termination notice for the El Salvador designation by its 2026-09-09 end date and that a DHS spokesperson said current holders keep their protection until an announcement. A June 2026 proposed rule would limit discretionary work authorization for parolees and people granted deferred action, but no action ending DACA itself was found; a USCIS page (undated snapshot) says renewals continue while initial requests are not processed because of a court order. Congress has not repealed TPS or legislated parole standards.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14165 (published 2025-01-30, FR Doc. 2025-02015) directs DHS to end the CHNV categorical parole processes and to stop using CBP One to parole inadmissible aliens.

Executive Order 14159 (90 FR 8443) section 16 limits parole under INA 212(d)(5) to case-by-case use for urgent humanitarian reasons or significant public benefit and directs that TPS designations be narrowly scoped and last only as long as the statute requires.
DHS publishes the termination of the October 2023 Venezuela TPS designation (90 FR 9040), effective 2025-04-07, affecting about 348,202 people.
DHS publishes a notice terminating the parole processes for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans and Venezuelans and their immediate family members, as of 2025-03-25 (FR Doc. 2025-05128).

DHS publishes a notice ending nine Family Reunification Parole programs (2023 programs for Colombians, Cubans, Ecuadorians, Guatemalans, Haitians, Hondurans and Salvadorans and legacy Cuban and Haitian programs), as of 2025-12-15, and revoking related employment authorization (FR Doc. 2025-22744).

Supreme Court decides Mullin v. Doe (No. 25-1083, consolidated with Trump v. Miot, No. 25-1084), 6 to 3, holding the TPS judicial-review bar prevents review of non-constitutional challenges to terminations, finding the Haiti equal protection claim unlikely to succeed on interim review, reversing the orders below and remanding.
The Supreme Court granted certiorari in Mullin v. National TPS Alliance (No. 26-48), vacated the Ninth Circuit judgment and remanded for further consideration in light of Mullin v. Doe.
